newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends on its lows after option selling.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends on its lows after option selling.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed on its lows on Wednesday as option-related selling out of Asia weighed on the kiwi.
It ended at 5.00 p.m. (0500 GMT) at US$0.6930/37 from its 0.6943/50 opening, after trading a 0.6932-53 range.
Dealers said the kiwi had a heavy tone as the Asian selling impacted on a relatively thin market.
But comments from the Reserve Bank on Monday that monetary conditions were too soft had provided the currency with a strong underpinning.
One dealer said he felt the wider market was still short and that would limit any downside.
The Australian dollar held important support at US$0.7755-60 after being thumped overnight on the budget news. That had helped the kiwi to its highs for the session.
On the Trade-Weighted currency index the New Zealand dollar ended at 67.84 from 67.91 at the opening.
